elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: § 11.1 as rendered: "Customer may terminate this Agreement during the Term upon at least ninety (90) days' written notice to M&I" — an unconditional Customer election, i.e. a convenience right.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: Rendered § 11.1 requires "at least ninety (90) days' written notice", not 30 days.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: No refund obligation appears anywhere in the rendered language; § 11.1 only imposes a payment obligation on Customer (the Termination for Convenience Fee) and says nothing about prepaid fees.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Rendered § 10.2: "M&I may, effective only at the end of the Term, withdraw any of the Services (other than the Core Services)..." — the former "at any time" mid-term withdrawal right is removed; the retained second sentence is a regulatory/judicial trigger, not convenience.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Rendered § 11.1 sets Customer's notice at "at least ninety (90) days' written notice", inside the 60–90 day band (down from one year in p0187).

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Fee is now "an amount equal to three (3) months of the average monthly Fees payable by Customer during the three-month period prior to Customer's notice", and the original add-on sentence for "unamortized Conversion or other costs, reasonable Expenses in connection with the disposition of equipment..." is deleted, so no uncapped Estimated-Remaining-Value or cost tail survives.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Rendered § 10.2 inserts "effective only at the end of the Term" before the withdrawal right, eliminating the mid-term partial convenience withdrawal; no other Vendor no-cause right appears in the cited text.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Already met and preserved: § 10.2 retains "upon providing ninety (90) days' prior written notice to Customer."

reasons: Fallback is position-complete: 90 days' Customer notice (§ 11.1), fee capped at three months' average monthly Fees with the unamortized-Conversion/Expenses add-on deleted, Vendor withdrawal limited to the end of the Term, and the existing 90-day Vendor notice retained.

Preferred fails on two elements: notice remains 90 days rather than 30, and no pro-rata prepaid-fee refund obligation is inserted. The drafter's decision to target the fallback is therefore correctly declared.

Minimality defect: the inserted sentence "The Termination for Convenience Fee shall be Customer's sole payment obligation arising from such termination." is an extra beyond the chosen checklist. The cap element is already achieved by the new three-month formula plus deletion of the unamortized-costs/Expenses sentence; the added sentence goes further and purports to extinguish all other termination-related payment obligations (e.g. accrued Fees, deconversion/transition assistance charges) that are not part of the early-termination fee. Delete that sentence to restore minimality.

No dangling terms or broken cross-references: the "Estimated Remaining Value" definition (p0039) is retained unchanged and still supports the Termination for Cause Fee, § 11.2(A) and § 13.5 continue to read coherently against the renamed-but-still-existing Termination for Convenience Fee, and the retained carve-outs (no fee on an Event of Default or under § 11.3) and the § 13.4 exclusion sentence are untouched, so allocation, timing and commercial mechanics survive.

Severity remains high: the original clause (one year's notice plus an uncapped Estimated-Remaining-Value exit charge on an eight-year term, expressly outside the § 13.4 cap) is a genuine fallback failure, and the pre-edit § 10.2 mid-term withdrawal right on 90 days' notice is an independent Vendor-side convenience defect.
